Excellent work, everyone. The picture is now clear, and I think we have everything we need to move forward. Let me synthesize the full set of issues and next steps for the approval package.

First, on exclusivity scope: Martin's prior grant to the University Research Consortium means our exclusive license must include a carveout preserving the consortium's existing academic research and teaching use rights. Martin will draft that carveout in coordination with Nora so it's consistent with the export-controls provisions.

Second, on royalty rate: Sofia's benchmark shows a 2.25% approved market ceiling, and we're currently at 3%. Combined with Daniel's title risk and Martin's carveout, the case for adjusting to or below 2.25% is strong. Sofia will prepare three financial scenarios — full portfolio, continuation carved out, and continuation carved out plus consortium carveout limited to originally assigned applications.

Third, on patent title: Daniel will circulate his title memorandum today, and we'll ask Northlake by tomorrow whether they can produce the missing assignment by Friday. If not, we pursue either a carve-out with adjusted pricing or a post-signing condition with a cure period. Daniel will also address whether the consortium's prior grant extends to the continuation application.

Fourth, on export controls: Nora will draft the military end-user prohibition and annual end-use screening certification language, scoped to work with Martin's carveout and prevent unintended channels for ECCN 3A001 technology to reach unscreened parties.

Tomorrow's discussion with Northlake needs to cover three questions: (1) can they produce the missing inventor assignment by Friday, (2) does the consortium's prior grant expressly reference the continuation application or is it limited to the originally assigned applications, and (3) are they willing to adjust the royalty rate to reflect the 2.25% market ceiling given the encumbrances and title risk. I need Martin's carveout language, Daniel's title memorandum, Sofia's three financial scenarios, and Nora's export-controls language all circulated by end of day today so we're fully prepared. Once we hear back from Northlake tomorrow, I'll make the final call on the approval package and the revised draft terms for Monday's signature.
